mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over the prior 8 weeks reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 8 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day rolling mean during the high-rate period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the labor signal meeting the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not in observable list, so skip) — instead: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 1% for three consecutive months indicates expanding supply-side demand, which typically precedes equity market optimism and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for two months followed by a sustained rise above 3% suggests the Federal Reserve is shifting policy, creating volatility in equity pricing and often producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3% for two consecutive months then crosses above 3%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during the inflation spike (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the federal funds rate exceeds +0.25 percentage points and persists for 4 months, it indicates aggressive monetary easing that lowers real interest rates, thereby supporting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > +0.25pp for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant deviation from the 30-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (not directly observable) — instead: A sharp decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a sustained stay below 4% for two months suggests a tight labor market, which can fuel wage growth and equity risk appetite, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE drops below 4% and remains below for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE remaining below 4% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in retail sales proxy (not available) — instead: A two-month rise in consumer confidence index (not available) — instead: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month average of 105.0 suggests accelerating demand, which typically precedes equity market strength and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the supply-side inflation pressure (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 4% for three consecutive months while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 6%, it indicates a supply shock that typically leads to equity market corrections and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% for three consecutive months and UNRATE < 6%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the inflation-unemployment condition (t-test p > 0.05).
